title: Hierarchical KV page-slicing and deferred reconstruction proposal
creator: Lena Zhang
description:
Background:

We currently manage the KV (key-value) activation cache using monolithic page units which leads to fragmentation when large activation ranges are sparsely used across batches. This increases GPU memory pressure and causes expensive whole-page swaps during oversubscription. Existing proposals in the repo focus on eviction heuristics, block allocators, and host-prefetching around whole page boundaries.

Goal:

Introduce a hierarchical page-slicing mechanism that allows a single 'page' to be split into variable-size slices (micro-pages) and support deferred reconstruction of contiguous activation ranges at the time of decode. Combined with a lightweight slice directory, the system should: 
- reduce wasted resident memory by enabling fine-grained residency for partial hotsets
- avoid immediate expensive recomposition of slices on miss by deferring reconstruction until the decode kernel actually needs contiguous KV ranges
- remain compatible with continuous batching and token-affinity optimizations

Non-goals:
- This PR does not aim to replace the global eviction policy or the batching scheduler.
- Not targeting multi-GPU sharding changes in this iteration; single-GPU and host-staged variants only.

Design overview:

1) Slice Directory: a compact host-resident index per model that maps (page_id, slice_offset) -> slice_descriptor (resident_location, length, version). Implemented as a fixed-size hash table with open addressing and epoch-based tombstones. The directory is intentionally small (a few KB) to retain cacheability in the control plane thread.

2) Micro-pages: logical subdivisions of a page (e.g., 512B-8KB depending on model token geometry). Pages are still the atomic unit for long-term on-disk/host staging; micro-pages allow selective residency.

3) Deferred Reconstruction: when a decode requires a contiguous KV span that crosses multiple resident micro-pages and some are missing, we enqueue a reconstruction task that:
   - merges resident micro-pages and pulls missing micro-pages from host staging into a temporary reconstruction buffer (pinned host or ephemeral GPU buffer depending on size),
   - performs a lightweight stitch step in CUDA that produces the contiguous KV segments required by the decoder kernel,
   - updates the slice directory atomically for future hits.

4) Fast-path for small token affinities: if the decode only needs micro-pages that are already resident, proceed without any stitching; this keeps the common low-latency path unchanged.

API/config knobs:

- slice_size_hint: integer (bytes) default 4096 -> used to pick micro-page sizing per model at load time
- reconstruction_budget_ms: integer default 2 -> time budget for inline reconstruction before deferring to background worker
- slice_eviction_granularity: enum {micro, page} default micro -> controls eviction unit under pressure

Telemetry and observability:

Emit the following counters/histograms:
- slice_hit_rate (per-model, per-seq-len bucket)
- reconstruction_latency_ms (P50/P95/P99)
- memory_wasted_by_page_internal_fragmentation_bytes
- resident_slice_count and resident_page_count
- percent_decodes_triggering_reconstruction

Benchmarks and evaluation plan:

1) Synthetic microbench: simulate a mix of decoding traffic with varying token affinities to measure resident memory vs page-based baseline. Key metrics: tokens/sec, mean latency (token), P99 latency, and GPU resident bytes.
2) Replay traces from production (small-talk conversational workload and long-form generation) to estimate effect on cost and tail latency.
3) Stress test oversubscription: force >1.4x resident demand and compare OOM rate and graceful-fallback behavior.

Rollout strategy:

- Stage 1 (canary): enable slice directory in host-staged mode only, slice_eviction_granularity=page, reconstruction off. Observe telemetry for regressions.
- Stage 2 (opt-in): enable micro slicing and deferred reconstruction behind runtime flag; limited to a small set of tenants with low latency requirements.
- Stage 3 (ramp): broader rollout with adaptive slice_size_hint tuning based on observed fragmentation metrics.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Reconstruction can increase tail latency for cold spans. Mitigation: reconstruction_budget_ms and background worker fallback; also dynamic threshold to promote frequently reconstructed spans to resident whole pages.
- Risk: Complexity blowup and lock contention on the slice directory. Mitigation: per-core partitioned directories and epoch GC to avoid global locks.
- Risk: Memory churn from temporary reconstruction buffers. Mitigation: bounded pooled buffers and prefer pinned host staging for large reconstructions.

Compatibility notes:

- The decoding path is backwards compatible: if slice metadata is absent, runtime falls back to page-based fetch.
- Host-staged and dedicated modes supported first; private on-prem may require tuning of slice_size_hint for different NICs and mmapped staging semantics.

Open questions:

- What are the correct heuristics to promote micro-pages back into full-page residency? Candidate signals: reconstruction frequency, slice_hit_rate, and decode-window overlap.
- Should slices be compressed in host staging to save bandwidth? Compression trade-offs need evaluation.
- Interaction with KV encryption/HSM: do we keep slices encrypted independently or at page-level?

Artifacts and references:

- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hierarchical+KV+Slicing
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2491
- Trace replays (GCS): gs://redwood-traces/2025-05-kv-frag-replays

Acceptance criteria:

- Correctness: no functional regression in token-level outputs for smoke tests.
- Memory reduction: >=15% reduction in resident bytes for the small-talk trace under nominal load.
- Latency: P99 decode latency increase <= 5% on steady-state traffic; any higher regressions must be explained and controlled by flags.
